title: Modeling approaches and criteria for appraising models
status: reviewed and locally validated; passes 1-9 complete; gate 6b round 2 had 1 blocking defect, fixed by the lead and checked by the lead (no round 3)
transcript_provenance: Local machine transcription (faster-whisper small.en); not publisher captions
source_uncertainties: Unverified (named in reader text, not opened): Pope, Turbulent Flows (2000), the apparent source of the module. The five criteria, the definition of completeness and the k-epsilon and mixing-length examples are checked only through Pope (2004), which cites the book as its reference [5]; no page of the book is cited.

The Source slide of Lecture 43 is not captured by the 30-second frames: f0004 to f0007 show slide 5 of 46 (the challenges slide) while the audio at 3:07 attributes the module to Pope. The attribution rests on the audio and on Pope (2004).

L43 13:55 says the dissipation rate is a single quantity with no mean; the slide lists it among the mean quantities and the definition used in this book is an ensemble average. Treated as a spoken slip.
L45 11:15 and 14:55 state exaflops as 10^15; the SI prefix exa is 10^18 and peta is 10^15. The slide table stops at tera. The chapter uses the SI prefixes.
L44 4:30 attributes a warning to Boussinesq; not checked. L44 6:01-7:15 links the mixing-length analogy to the energy cascade; the chapter keeps the two apart.

L45 3:19 says the mixing-length model is incomplete because its constants come from empirical relations; the checked definition (Pope 2004 p. 7) is a flow-dependent specification. The chapter states both.
ASR spellings: 'business hypothesis' for Boussinesq, 'Rana stresses', 'RAMS' and 'RANs' for RANS, 'Re cubed' for Re^3, 'Reynolds average Avi Stokes'. The chapter follows the slides.

The slide table header reads 'number of directions of statistical homogeneity' while its examples fit the number of directions of statistical inhomogeneity; the chapter follows the examples and the lecture's wording (L44 18:40).
The speed-against-year slide (f0030) axis reads 'Peak speed (Rmax)'; the chapter does not use the label. The TOP500 country ranking (June 2016) is not used.

Specification constants in the channel calculation (kappa 0.41, fraction 0.07, specification B) are assumed inputs without a source; they illustrate the dependence on the specification and are not a calibration.

Lee and Moser (2015): the grid sizes are quoted from the data-file headers; the journal paper was not read, so whether nx and nz count collocation points or Fourier modes is not stated by the chapter.

sections.section: The objects of the chapter and the running case
sections.lecture_material: Definitions of simulation (a field for one realization) and model (equations for mean quantities) as used in L43 1:27-2:17.
sections.research_extension: Pope (2004) pp. 2-3 and 6: LES as a resolved field and as a physical model.
sections.teaching_construction: The channel of chapter 9 (Re_tau 1000.5, d 2 cm, nu 1e-6 m^2/s) as the running case with the two client questions.

sections.section: The turbulence problem and three ways to compute around it
sections.lecture_material: Objective and the four difficulties (slide f0008); DNS, LES and RANS as defined on slide f0049; the cost and accuracy ordering (L43 23:10-24:40, repeated L44 1:18-1:40).
sections.research_extension: Pope (2004) p. 8: resolution measure M = k_r/(k_res + k_r), M = 0 DNS, M = 1 RANS; pp. 3-4: cases where LES has less advantage; L45 accuracy slide: DNS removes only the model error.
sections.teaching_construction: Table 16.1, Figure 16.1, the qualification of the accuracy ordering, the correction that epsilon is already an average.

sections.section: How the cost of a direct simulation grows with the Reynolds number
sections.lecture_material: Slide: DNS cost increases as Re^3, restricted to low-to-moderate Re; example Re 100 to 1000 gives a factor 1000.
sections.research_extension: Pope (2004) p. 13: LES cost ~ (L/Delta)^4, comparable with DNS for Delta ~ eta; Lee and Moser (2015) data-file headers: grids and Re_tau.
sections.teaching_construction: Reference to chapter 5 for the derivation; local grid exponents 2.27 and 2.38 against 9/4 as a consistency check; memory of one snapshot (14, 58, 2899 GB).

sections.section: Five criteria and two extreme cases
sections.lecture_material: Slide f0051: five criteria; mixing-length model and DNS as two extremes; question of how complete LES and RANS are (L43 25:40).
sections.research_extension: Pope (2004) p. 15: the same five criteria, attributed to Pope (2000); additional LES-only convergence requirement not added to the list.

sections.section: The mixing-length model: one algebraic relation closes the mean equations
sections.lecture_material: Slide f0010: <uv> = -nu_T dU/dy, nu_T = l_m^2 |dU/dy|, l_m specified as a function of position; Boussinesq remark, kinetic-theory analogy, fraction of the flow length (L44 4:12-7:35).
sections.research_extension: Chapter 9 (9.13), (9.27) and the Boussinesq attribution (Schmitt 2007 through chapter 9).
sections.teaching_construction: Equations (16.5)-(16.7): the channel reduction, the quadratic in dU+/dy+ and its positive root; separation of the momentum-transport analogy from the energy cascade.

sections.lecture_material: Slide f0019: DNS gives U(x,t) and all statistics; mixing length gives <U>, <V> only; the mean-flow description is adequate in many applications; speaker's grading of the mixing-length model.
sections.teaching_construction: The ladder of statistics of chapters 7-9, and the pressure-gradient and velocity-probability questions for the running case.

sections.lecture_material: Slide f0027: definition of completeness, DNS complete, mixing length incomplete, incomplete models useful for narrow classes; L45 2:38-3:42 recap with the statement that constants come from empirical relations.
sections.research_extension: Pope (2004) p. 7: the same definition, k-epsilon complete, mixing length incomplete, two practitioners differ; pp. 7-8: LES as practised is incomplete, adaptive LES.
sections.teaching_construction: Table 16.2: three specifications of l_m in the channel; separation of flow-dependent specification from boundary conditions and of constants from specifications.

sections.lecture_material: Slide f0040: table of flows by statistical dimensionality; difficulty rules; Re dependence (DNS versus mixing length); two-part task (program, execution); L45 4:41-9:00 repeat and the validation effort.
sections.research_extension: Lee and Moser (2015) headers for the DNS grid of a statistically one-dimensional flow.
sections.teaching_construction: Table 16.3 and the reading of its row index; the scope of the table (mean-flow calculations); grid convergence of the mean-flow integral (101 and 401 points).

sections.section: Computer speed and the range of direct simulation
sections.lecture_material: Slide f0023: table of speeds 1963-1998, a factor of 30 per decade, 1000 in 20 years, caution on achieved speed; f0030 and f0032: speed against year and TOP500 curves; speaker's exaflops 10^15 slip.
sections.teaching_construction: Least-squares fit of the table (27.7 per decade, 769 in 20 years); equation (16.8), growth of the reachable Reynolds number as F_10^(1/3) per decade.

sections.lecture_material: Slide f0036: models for homogeneous turbulence, mixing-length geometry restriction, DNS limited by Re, applicability different from accuracy.
sections.teaching_construction: Overlap between completeness and applicability for an incomplete model.

sections.lecture_material: Slide f0050: accuracy by comparison with experiment, boundary conditions, four sources of discrepancy, truncation error and cost; the jet and nozzle example (L45 21:15-26:18).
sections.research_extension: Pope (2004) pp. 5-6 and 15: cost of halving the grid spacing is about 2^4 = 16; T = c (L/Delta)^4.
sections.teaching_construction: Equation (16.9), cost proportional to the truncation error to the power -4/n; Table 16.4; the inference that the inlet specification grows with the level of description.

sections.section: Where large-eddy simulation sits on the five criteria
sections.lecture_material: L43 21:00-21:30: LES as the filtered velocity of one realization.
sections.research_extension: Pope (2004) pp. 3-4, 7-13, 15: statistical relationship of the resolved field to the velocity, Q_m(Delta), intermediate asymptote hypothesis, cost, completeness, range.
sections.teaching_construction: Placement of Pope's statements on the lecture's five criteria.
Program ch16_models.py: mixing-length channel integral, flops fit, grid exponents, error-cost relation, exercise numbers, memory and grid convergence.

sections.section: What the criteria establish and what they do not
sections.teaching_construction: Limits of the ordering, of the scaling, of Table 16.2, of the speaker's judgments and of the Pope (2000) attribution.
Six exercises: derive and compute, judge, check an assumption, design, derive and compute, derive.

symbol_ledger.definition: Pope's resolution measure (16.1): residual over total turbulent kinetic energy (the source writes K for the resolved energy).
u_0 l_0 / nu, the Reynolds number of the energy-containing eddies (chapter 10); the slide writes Re.
Reynolds shear stress (the <u_1 u_2> of chapter 9), turbulent viscosity, mixing length; the slide writes l_m.
dU+/dy+ and l_m u_tau / nu in the channel reduction.
Computer speed in flop/s and its growth factor F_10 in ten years (written F_10 because G is the LES filter kernel of NOTATION.md).
Truncation error and its exponent in (Delta x)^n.
Turbulence-resolution length, resolved field, a statistic and its LES estimate (Pope 2004). Pope's integral length scale L is written ell_0 here.
